# One-coordinate facet roofs: strict deficit and explicit affine extraction

This is an ordinary all-dimensional first-variation theorem in a
specified class of convex-body deformations. It is independent of the
mixed seven-base response examples and does not resolve OC.

Let d>=2, m=d+1, b=1/m, h=d/m, Gamma=h^d. On a (d-1)-simplex F use
barycentrics s_1,...,s_d and its normalized uniform probability law P.
Define the bounded multiplicity function

    N(s)=number of indices i with s_i>=b.

Boundary conventions on these hyperplanes do not affect integrals.
For an integrable function psi define its facet deficit by

    E_d(psi)=int_F [N(s)-m Gamma] psi(s) dP(s).       (1)

This functional vanishes on every affine psi. Indeed by symmetry
E[N]=d h^(d-1)=m Gamma and E[N s_i]=E[N]/d, whereas E[s_i]=1/d.

## 1. Exact hinge deficits

For 0<c<1 put psi_c(s)=min(s_1,c). Its deficit E(c)=E_d(psi_c) is
strictly positive. More precisely, set

    I_L(c)= c L^(d-1)/(d-1)
              -[L^d-(L-c)_+^d]/[d(d-1)]  for c>=0,
    I_L(c)=0 for c<0.

Then the exact formula is

    E(c)=m Gamma(d-1) I_1(c)
            -(d-1) I_h(c-b)-(d-1)^2 I_h(c).         (2)

To prove it, the marginal X=s_1 has density
(d-1)(1-x)^(d-2), x in[0,1]. Conditional on X=x, its own indicator
in N is 1_(x>=b). Each of the other d-1 coordinates exceeds b
with probability ((h-x)_+/(1-x))^(d-2), with the natural indicator
interpretation when d=2. Thus the density-weighted conditional value
of N-m Gamma is

    (d-1)(1-x)^(d-2)[1_(x>=b)-m Gamma]
            +(d-1)^2(h-x)_+^(d-2).                 (3)

When d=2, the final term is (d-1)^2 1_(x<h); its value at x=h is
irrelevant. Since E_d annihilates constants and min(x,c)=c-(c-x)_+,
integration of (3) gives (2). The function I_L is exactly
int_0^min(c,L)(c-x)(L-x)^(d-2)dx, as direct differentiation shows.

For c>=b, simplifying (2) gives

    E(c)=[h^(d-1)-1/d](1-c)^d
                         -(d-1)(h-c)_+^d/d.        (4)

For 0<=c<=b, one has E(0)=E'(0)=0 and

    E''(c)=(d-1)(1-c)^(d-2)
       [d h^(d-1)-(d-1)((h-c)/(1-c))^(d-2)]
       >= [h^(d-2)/m](d-1)(1-c)^(d-2)>0.           (5)

The inequality uses (h-c)/(1-c)<=h and
d h-(d-1)=1/m. It remains valid for d=2. Therefore E(c)>0 for
0<c<=b. On[b,1), division of (4) by (1-c)^d gives an increasing
function, because (h-c)_+/(1-c) decreases. It starts strictly positive
at b, proving positivity throughout the interval without an asymptotic
or unproved numerical inequality.

## 2. A quantitative affine majorant for every concave one-variable roof

Define the explicit dimension-only constants

    k_1=h^(d-2)/m,
    k_2=d h^(d-1)-1-(d-1)((d-1)/d)^d,
    k_d=min(k_1,k_2)>0.                             (6)

Positivity of k_2 follows from (4) at b and the strict positivity
just proved: k_2=d E(b)/(1-b)^d. No separate estimate is assumed.

For every continuous concave phi:[0,1]->[0,infinity), there exists
an explicitly defined affine function ell>=phi such that

    int_F [ell(s_1)-phi(s_1)] dP
                       <= E_d(phi(s_1))/k_d.       (7)

Moreover E_d(phi(s_1))=0 if and only if phi is affine.

First prove the estimate for a hinge. If c<=b, use the majorant
ell_c(x)=c. Its integrated error is
B(c)=(d-1) I_1(c). Both B and E vanish with their first derivatives
at zero, while (5) gives E''>=k_1 B''. Hence E(c)>=k_1 B(c).
If c>=b, use ell_c(x)=x. Its error is

    int (X-c)_+ dP=(1-c)^d/d.

Formula (4) and the monotonicity after it give E(c) at least k_2
times that error. This proves (7) for each hinge with the SAME k_d.

For completeness, the general concave function has the Green-kernel
representation

    phi(x)=(1-x)phi(0)+x phi(1)
                +int_(0,1) G_c(x) dmu(c),
    G_c(x)=min(x,c)-cx,
    mu=-phi'' in the distributional sense.           (8)

Here mu is a positive locally finite measure. One elementary proof
first verifies the formula by matching slope jumps for piecewise
linear concave functions, then applies it on compact interior
intervals to the monotone derivative and takes endpoint limits.
Continuity of phi at the endpoints gives the displayed zero-boundary
Green representation. Its integrals are finite: at any fixed interior
x, G_c(x) is a positive constant times c near0 and times(1-c) near1.
Thus int_0^b c dmu and int_b^1(1-c)dmu are finite.

Replace G_c(x) in (8) by the affine majorant

    L_c(x)=c(1-x) if c<=b,
    L_c(x)=(1-c)x if c>b,

and call the resulting affine function ell. The preceding integrability
makes ell finite; all its endpoint values are nonnegative. It majorizes
phi pointwise. Since (1) kills affine terms,

    E_d(phi(s_1))=int E(c) dmu(c),
    int_F(ell-phi)dP=int int_F(L_c-G_c)dP dmu(c).

These interchanges are legitimate: G_c is nonnegative, its mixture
has finite integral, and |N-m Gamma| is bounded, giving absolute
integrability for the signed first identity. Tonelli applies to the
second. Integrating the hinge inequalities proves (7). Strict
positivity of E(c) for every interior c makes equality possible
only when mu=0, that is, when phi is affine.

## 3. Actual simplex facet deformation and first variation

Let T be the standard d-simplex, of volume V=1/d!, and parameterize
it by z=(z_1,...,z_(d-1)) in the standard (d-1)-simplex Delta and
a vertical coordinate r:

    z_j>=0, sum z_j<=1,
    sum z_j-1<=r<=0.

The affine map to standard coordinates is
(z,r)->(z_1,...,z_(d-1),1-sum z_j+r), with determinant one.
On its top facet, s_1=z_1 and the remaining facet barycentrics
are z_2,...,z_(d-1),1-sum z_j.

For a fixed continuous nonnegative concave phi, not identically zero,
define the actual convex body

    K_epsilon={z in Delta:
                  sum z_j-1<=r<=epsilon phi(z_1)}. (9)

Convexity follows from the concavity of its roof and its affine floor.
The added volume is epsilon W int_F phi(s_1)dP, where
W=1/(d-1)!=d V. Its normalized added law tends to the facet law
with density proportional to phi(s_1). Every canonical centroid
hyperplane has zero mass under that limiting law, since phi is bounded
and the uniform facet measure gives its proper hyperplane traces zero
measure. The hyperplane for the opposite original vertex does not
meet that facet at its centroid threshold.

The proved ordinary weak-added-law first-variation theorem therefore
gives the normalized MAXIMUM depth

    D(K_epsilon)=Gamma+epsilon[d/m] E_d(phi(s_1))
                                                +o(epsilon). (10)

All point selection and all-direction issues are contained in that
separately audited theorem. The coefficient follows by summing the
canonical indicator masses N and then normalizing by the new total
volume. It is strictly positive for every nonaffine phi by Section2.

## 4. An explicit enclosing simplex controls the residual to first order

Let ell(x)=A+Bx be the affine majorant from Section2 and let

    S_epsilon={z_j>=0:
           sum z_j-1<=r<=epsilon(A+Bz_1)}.          (11)

For small epsilon with 1-epsilon B>0 this is a full-dimensional
simplex containing K_epsilon. To see boundedness and its simplex
form, set q=r-sum z_j+1>=0. The upper constraint becomes

    q+(1-epsilon B)z_1+sum_(j>=2)z_j<=1+epsilon A,

with every coefficient positive. No optimizing affine simplex is
assumed to exist.

Above z in Delta, its exact missing volume is
epsilon W int_F(ell-phi)dP. The extra part with sum z_j>1 has
volume O_phi(epsilon^2), as can be verified without a boundary-layer
estimate from the EXACT total-volume formulas

    |S_epsilon|=V(1+epsilon A)^d/(1-epsilon B),
    |K_epsilon|=V+epsilon d V int_F phi(s_1)dP.

The simplex formula follows by scaling its displayed positive
coordinate coefficients. Since int_F ell(s_1)dP=A+B/d, expansion
of this rational expression proves

    1-|K_epsilon|/|S_epsilon|
        =epsilon d int_F(ell-phi)dP+O_phi(epsilon^2)
        <=epsilon(d/k_d) E_d(phi)+O_phi(epsilon^2). (12)

For nested uniform-body laws their total variation is exactly the
relative missing volume; their halfspace-cap distance is no larger.
When phi is nonaffine, (10)-(12) imply

    liminf_(epsilon->0)
       [D(K_epsilon)-Gamma]
           /[1-|K_epsilon|/|S_epsilon|] >=k_d/m,    (13)

and the same lower ratio bound holds with the infimum cap distance
to all affine simplices in the denominator. As usual a zero
denominator creates no counterexample to the bound. For every fixed
c<k_d/m the corresponding inequality holds for all sufficiently
small epsilon, with a threshold allowed to depend on phi.

The affine-roof case has zero first variation and is not assigned a
positive first-order residual bound by this statement. Uniform
relative remainders for roofs varying with epsilon are also NOT
claimed. This theorem concerns one-coordinate facet roofs; general
concave roofs on a facet of dimension at least two require a new
argument. None of these ordinary comparisons proves mixed OC.
